input.quote: IBM may cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time. In the event IBM cancels Purchase Order as the result of MSL's default, no cancellation charge shall be applicable. IBM's termination of Purchase Orders for its convenience shall not relieve IBM of any cost reimbursements under the Price section.
input.rationale: The only convenience mechanic in the deal is the quoted SOW Section 6.1, which reaches individual Purchase Orders and still leaves IBM liable for cost reimbursements; it does not let IBM exit the Agreement. The Base Agreement runs three years (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination only for cause - breach, insolvency, competitor acquisition, or continuing force majeure (p0107 to p0118). Section 4.0's six-month notice is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL, not T4C). Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is a missing-behaviour deviation, so we insert operative language: 'IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL', with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. I re-checked the cross-reference: the retained for-cause preamble sits under the heading paragraph '5.1 Breach' (p0106), so 'Notwithstanding Section 5.1' is not dangling; that narrow opener avoids rewriting Section 5.1. Direction is checked - MSL has no mid-term convenience right, so preferred element 4 is already met and no new restriction on MSL is drafted. 60 to 90 days' notice remains the fallback concession.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 5.4: IBM convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, prevailing over the Section 5.1 for-cause preamble
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5.0 today allows exit only for cause, leaving us locked into a three-year term, so we have added Section 5.4 under which IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience on thirty (30) days' prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. The narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" opener keeps the for-cause rights intact while ensuring that preamble is not read as an exclusive list; we can move to 60-90 days' notice as our fallback.

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience by IBM. Notwithstanding Section 5.1, IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
